parallel.requirements: Port test11.cpp to Rust, preserve all eleven idna API outputs and CLI defaults byte-for-byte, use only std, and create a Cargo project plus test11.rs in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and build, then delegated post-build verification to a workflow with spec, fuzz, and critic phases across 19 child logs.
parallel.implementation: Implemented byte-oriented idna behavior in modular Rust files, including unconditional xn-- prefixing, one-prefix stripping, byte length validators, ASCII folding, and dot counting.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Assembled Cargo.toml, test11.rs, src/lib.rs, src/idna modules, and a compiled test11 executable; artifact validation found the expected entry and output tree.
parallel.verification: Ran local differential checks, then launched a broad verifier workflow; completed spec agents reported matches and several fuzz agents returned, but aggregate workflow result was null.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official correctness defect remained because evaluation passed 40/40, but the verifier workflow was killed, two fuzz agents were still in progress, and final.txt was empty after timeout.

serial.requirements: Used the identical prompt constraints and inferred the same eleven-function stub behavior from the compiled C++ binary while keeping the project dependency-free.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single parent handled probing, implementation, build repair, unit tests, differential fuzzing, artifact check, and final report without delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented an accepted Rust Cargo project with modules for args, ascii, punycode, validation, and idna entry points, including raw-byte argv handling for byte-faithful behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created the final /output project, compiled test11 and target/release/test11, and listed the expected tree before closing.
serial.verification: Ran rustc, cargo build, cargo test, 54 curated cases, 1200 randomized cases, 400 raw-byte cases, and 200 multi-argument cases, then official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official task failure is evidenced; the final report notes a deliberate args_os deviation from the literal std::env::args wording to preserve invalid UTF-8 bytes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the same porting task: implement all eleven idna APIs, preserve CLI defaults and byte-for-byte stdout, use only std, and place a Cargo project plus test11.rs in /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same task and constraints from the identical prompt, including black-box inference from the compiled C++ binary and no external crates.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference; both runs targeted the full required API surface and output contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent owned implementation and then delegated post-build verification to a broad workflow with per-API spec agents, fuzz agents, and a critic.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent kept implementation, probing, build, fuzzing, and reporting in one local trajectory without delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Implementation ownership was adequate in both; only parallel split verification into many children, creating later closure pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Verifier children received a detailed common script with C++ and Rust binary paths, read-only /output rules, byte-exact comparison requirements, and structured return schemas.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interface boundary; the parent directly used the prompt, binary probes, local files, and final tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No context omission or incompatible interface is evidenced; the important coordination boundary was the breadth and lifecycle of verifier work, not missing task facts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote a std-only Cargo project with modules under src/idna, test11.rs at the package root, and a built executable accepted as the expected artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent independently wrote a std-only Cargo project with analogous idna modules, fixed a rustc re-export issue, and built the required executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced functionally accepted byte-faithful implementations through similar black-box reverse engineering; file organization differs but not official behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After implementation the verifier workflow had result null and status killed, and the main process ended with return code 143 before writing a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its own verification, returned a final report, and the agent process exited with return code 0.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost normal result lifecycle closure after spawning the verifier workflow; serial delivered a normal final answer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent integrated the final project before verification; the verifier script instructed children not to modify /output, so no write collision is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and integrated its project directly in /output without concurrent writers or shared-state handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No merge or write-state failure explains the outcome; parallel shared-state risk was controlled by read-only verifier rules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local checks, then a large verifier workflow whose completed spec children found matches; official evaluation later passed all 40 testcases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo tests plus curated, randomized, raw-byte, and multi-argument differential checks, then official evaluation passed all 40 testcases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified enough for official acceptance; parallel verification was broader but did not finish as an aggregate workflow before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2400 second agent budget, recorded return code 143, zero remaining retry budget, process_ok false, and an empty final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished within the same budget with return code 0, 177 seconds remaining, process_ok true, and a normal final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete task-solving process difference: accepted artifacts in both modes, but parallel spent closure budget on verifier fan-out while serial stopped cleanly.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial passed 40/40. The concrete difference is process closure. Parallel produced an accepted artifact, then spent the remainder of the budget on a broad verifier workflow that was killed before an aggregate result or final answer. Serial produced an accepted artifact and normal final report within budget.
parallel_contributors: Accepted artifact was built before timeout.
Broad verifier workflow consumed remaining run budget and prevented normal final response.
serial_contributors: Accepted artifact was built and verified locally.
No delegation overhead; process exited normally with 177 seconds remaining and a final report.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary implementation defect explains an outcome difference because both official evaluations passed.
Serial explicitly noted args_os instead of literal args() for invalid UTF-8; official tests accepted the behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence only

The indispensable implementation path was completed and accepted; the more specific event is collective verifier fan-out exhausting closure budget.

After producing an accepted artifact, the parent launched a verifier workflow with 11 spec agents and eight fuzz strategies; the 19-child workflow was killed with result null and the main process timed out with no final response.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier workflow did not return an aggregate result and the parallel run produced no final response before timeout, although the submitted artifact passed official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The absent verifier aggregate is downstream of the same broad fan-out budget exhaustion episode; no independent trapped verifier finding needs a separate result-lifecycle label.

Children were independent verifiers expected to return structured findings, not separately owned implementation components requiring an interoperability contract.

The parent did not receive an overly large completed handoff and fail to reduce it; the aggregate verifier result never arrived before timeout.
No receiver consumed a superseded workspace or requirement state; verifier children read the current built artifact.
Returned verifier reports did not create an unresolved integration conflict; reported SIGPIPE findings were peripheral to official acceptance and the workflow never reached final adjudication.
The parent did not make a final whole-task completion decision without checks; official evaluation passed and the run instead timed out before final response.
There is no replacement child or retry that lacked inherited checkpoints and repeated prior work; repeated fuzz rounds were scripted verifier depth.
